verdict.rationale: Kong documents its own registrable outbound webhooks. Gateway Event Hooks can listen for create, delete or modify events on Gateway entities and POST them through `webhook` or `webhook-custom` handlers. Konnect separately offers audit-log webhooks with a status API. Coverage is fragmented: Event Hooks are on-prem only and limited to entity-change events, and the Konnect Notification Hub, which covers the broader set of org events, delivers only by email and in-app. missing for 10: a unified webhook subscription for Konnect platform events (Notification Hub has no webhook channel), event-type breadth beyond entity CRUD and audit logs, payload and delivery semantics (retries, signing), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: An Event Hook is a Kong Gateway entity that can be configured to listen for specific events from Kong Gateway entities. An Event Hook can be configured to send information to logs, webhooks, or third-party applications.
You can collect audit logs for both the Konnect org and Dev Portal using a webhook you configure.
Notifications are delivered through two supported channels: email and in-app (via the bell icon in the Konnect UI)
